source.what: The scanner's own ECG printout (3 secondary-capture images), digitized from pixels.
source.deidentified: Pixels contain no name, ID or date; no DICOM header field except series description and model is used.

calibration.amplitude: normalized: 0 = PR-segment baseline of each beat (interpolated between beats), 1 = median R-peak height

rhythm.note: Single-channel monitoring ECG from the scanner, not a diagnostic 12-lead ECG: no amplitude calibration, unknown filtering, 10 ms per pixel. PR is measured from the P-wave PEAK to QRS onset (shorter than a clinical PR interval, which starts at P onset).

assumptions: The 7 strip rows are one continuous recording, 400 px (4.0 s) per row. Evidence: the label '73' is split across the I1/I2 boundary, the trace level matches at every row join, and every R-R interval that spans a row break matches its printed heart rate (implied gaps ~0 px).

Time base: printed HR (RR = 60/HR) fitted against the spacing of the scanner's R markers gives 99.97 px/s (RMS residual 2 ms, within the 1 px marker quantisation), so the display runs at exactly 100 px/s = 10 ms per pixel.
Per-beat heart rates are the numbers the scanner printed (transcribed from zoomed renders); every one matches our own marker spacing within 2 bpm.
The trace is the centre of the white line in each pixel column. Steep QRS strokes are rebuilt from their extremes (R tip, Q/S troughs); columns hidden under a bar outline are interpolated.
Amplitude has no mV calibration (none is printed), so it is normalised to the median R-peak height.

Green bars: the dark-green band is drawn as the X-ray exposure window (centred at 75% of the scanner's predicted R-R, matching 'Scan Phase 75%'); the lighter outlined box inside it is most likely the image-data (reconstruction) window ('Recon Phase BestDiast 76%').

Table positions: the first three exposures cover -1819.8 to -1716.2 mm, the fourth -1716.2 to -1681.8 mm; they are split evenly per exposure (34.5 mm steps). Patient z (DICOM LPS) = -table position, which matches the calcium-score slices (z 1683.25-1818.25 mm, 3 mm thick).
R-peak times come from the digitized trace; the scanner's markers sit -24 ms earlier on average (it triggers on the R upstroke).
